newsitem.title: USA: Florida home resales rise one percent in February.
newsitem.headline: Florida home resales rise one percent in February.

text.p: Florida sales of existing single-family homes rose to 8,505 in February, a one-percent increase over Febuary of last year, the Florida Association of Realtors said Tuesday.
The median sales price increased by 2 percent to $91,200 over the year.

The association attributed the increase in sales to positive economic indicators and low interest rates. The average rate for a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage was 7.65 percent in February, compared to 7.08 percent a year ago and 7.82 percent in January 1997.

The Tampa and Orlando areas both saw significant gains, with home resales rising by more than eight percent over last year in Tampa and by seven percent in Orlando. Realtors credited strong job creation in both regions.
"We're almost at a shortage of listings, home sales here have been so great," said Jo Easton, president of the Greater Tampa Association of Realtors.
Orlando's home inventory was 10 percent lower than a year ago and "edging toward a seller's market," said Max Sabeti, president of the Greater Orlando Association of Realtors.
Orlando also saw gains in move-up buyers, new residents and South American and European buyers.
Among smaller markets, the Fort Myers-Cape Coral area and the Punta Gorda area both saw 30 percent gains over last February, partly due to out-of-state and foreign investment purchases.
Other areas showing gains were Gainseville, up 16 percent; Sarasota-Bradenton, up 13 percent; Pensacola, up eight percent; Naples, up six percent; and Melbourne-Titusville up one percent.

Areas posting declines from last February were Lakeland-Winter Haven, down 25 percent; Fort Walton Beach, down 16 percent; Tallahassee, down 11 percent; West Palm Beach, down 10 percent; Miami, down nine percent; Fort Lauderdale and Fort Pierce, both down eight percent; Jacksonville, down seven percent; Ocala, Daytona Beach and Panama City, each down three percent.
